description: Notes v2 three-way merge vectors (ADR-0035 amendment, docs/research/notes-v2-design-20260924.md section 4). Each vector gives the decrypted plaintext payloads base (last server-acknowledged), local (pending edit) and remote (pulled server row). expected is the merged payload exactly as the merging client serializes it, or {"conflict": true} when the merge must fall back to keeping both copies. Shared by the PC (Rust) and Android (Java) tests.
rules: Canonical serialization: keys schema, type, title, body, memo, color, labels, items, fields, pinned, deleted, archived, createdAt, updatedAt, then unknown keys. Absent: schema (v1), type when text, memo when none, color when none, labels when empty, items/fields when not that type, archived when false.
items and fields are sorted by (order, id) with plain code-unit comparison.

A checklist body is the GFM task list of open items then checked items, each group by (order, id); a secret body is 'label: value' lines by (order, id), then a blank line and memo when memo is non-empty. Newlines inside an item or field collapse to one space.

Scalars: the side that changed wins; both changed differently: title/type/text body/memo -> conflict; color/pinned -> remote; deleted/archived -> false; createdAt -> remote. updatedAt = max(local, remote). schema = max(local, remote), raised to 2 when v2 fields are present.
A type change on one side plus a body/memo/items/fields change on the other side is a conflict.

Items/fields per id: text/label/value collide -> conflict; checked/order collide -> remote. Deleted on one side: removed unless the other side changed text or checked (item) or label or value (field); a pure move does not keep it.
Labels per case-insensitive key: in base -> kept only if still on both sides; not in base -> kept if on either side. Order: remote labels, then local additions; the remote spelling wins.
Unknown keys (top level and per item/field) merge with the one-side rule; a collision takes remote.
Any side with schema > 2 or an unknown type -> conflict.

Ledger canonical serialization: ... fields, ledger, month, income, recurring, planned, entries, pinned ... (ledger: income, recurring, planned always present; ledger-month: ledger, month, income, entries always present and archived always true). Recurring keys id, name, amount, every, unit, start, trial, until, memo, order, forkOf?; planned id, name, amount, month, memo, dropped, order, forkOf?; entries id, date, amount, name, in (only when true), createdAt, recurring?, planned?, forkOf?; then unknown keys.

Ledger merges (type ledger or ledger-month) never keep a whole-note copy unless type, ledger or month differ on any side (conflict) or the result breaks a limit. title and income collisions take remote; body is regenerated; other scalars as above.

Ledger collections (recurring, planned, entries) merge per id. A field changed on one side wins; an order collision takes remote; an unknown-key collision takes remote; any other field collision forks the item: the remote version keeps the id, the local version is added with id = UUID v4 layout of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256('lakomics-ledger-fork:1:' + local note updatedAt + ':' + remote note updatedAt + ':' + id) and forkOf = id. Deleted on one side is removed unless the other side changed a field other than order. The same id added on both sides is kept once when equal apart from order (remote order), else forked.
